findings.claim: Objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is an endpoint pointcloud over predicted endpoint world coordinates with a fixed mixture temperature of 0.5 and teacher endpoint temperature 4.0.

Observed support spans the learning window 0.0-0.5 with 50 observed score times at 0.01 spacing; recorded affinities are removed and the label prior is equal-score, so selection preference is association evidence only, not measured final affinity benefit.

Across the 20 landmark soft-mass features, whole-window z magnitudes are small (largest about 0.64 for landmark_00_soft_mass) while first/last rate z values are large and of opposite sign for several landmarks (e.g. landmark_00 first_rate_z ~ +9.3, last_rate_z ~ -10.0; landmark_10 first_rate_z ~ +66.3, last_rate_z ~ -11.6; landmark_11 first_rate_z ~ -66.3, last_rate_z ~ +10.8), indicating changing contrasts rather than a stationary coordinate target.

Polynomial fits are not accepted for any of the 20 soft-mass trends, relative node RMSE is high (roughly 0.29-0.99), and sign changes range from 4 to 10 with strong sign conflicts up to 17, so no landmark soft-mass trajectory supports a stable monotone coordinate direction over the observed window.

hypotheses.direction: track the supplied validated contrast change; do not impose an absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient
hypotheses.falsifier: the regional term fails if the landmark_00 soft-mass contrast does not change sign within the observed window or if the whole-window z remains within noise while the rate z values lose their opposite-sign pattern
hypotheses.observable: landmark_00_soft_mass regional attention weight under the supplied Gaussian landmark attention with positive background
hypotheses.statement: A bounded regional coordinate reward on landmark_00 soft-mass attention, scoped to the observed window 0.0-0.5, may be defensible only as a contrast-tracking term because its whole-window mean shift is small while its early and late rates have opposite signs.

hypotheses.direction: retain incumbent rather than add a global absolute-coordinate target
hypotheses.falsifier: a global target would become supported only if a landmark soft-mass trend showed an accepted polynomial fit with a consistent whole-window z and no strong sign conflicts
hypotheses.observable: whole-window z and polynomial_accepted across all 20 landmark soft-mass continuous trends
hypotheses.statement: No global coordinate target should be derived from the soft-mass trends: the largest whole-window z is about 0.64 and all polynomial fits are rejected, so a global absolute-coordinate reward would be unsupported by the supplied evidence.

limitations: Recorded affinities are removed and the label prior is equal-score; selection preference is association evidence, not descendant survival or measured final affinity benefit.
No current-study outcome data are available to either role, so no hypothesis here can be validated against final predicted affinity.
Soft-mass features are untyped coordinate proxies in predicted endpoint world coordinates; they are not physical interaction energies or evidence of neural-module causation.
Temporal rate contrasts do not by themselves specify an absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient, so no absolute target is proposed.
Temperatures (mixture 0.5, teacher endpoint 4.0) are immutable task parameters and are not proposed for edit.
